messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sengupta <priya.s@nebulaanalytics.com>, Jake Montero <jake@nebulaanalytics.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Nebula Analytics - Hosted API degraded (status page + follow-up)

Hi Priya / Jake —

We’re seeing a degradation affecting the Redwood hosted text-generation API that’s impacting a subset of customer requests in us-west-2; response times are elevated and some requests are returning 502/timeout errors. We’ve posted an incident on the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/20260214-nebula.

Immediate items we’re doing now:
- Rotating a traffic bucket to a dedicated capacity pool to reduce contention.
- Rolling back a recent kernel tweak for the transformer runtime suspected to be amplifying latency for long-sequence calls.
- Increasing logging and capturing full request traces for your tenant to help scope exactly what failed.

We don’t have a complete root cause yet; I wanted to notify you ASAP and give an initial mitigation timeline (~30–60 minutes for routing changes to take effect).

Can you confirm what workloads you’re seeing failures on (ad-hoc live queries vs scheduled batch jobs)? That will help prioritize routing decisions. We’ll follow up with a short timeline/ETA and a post-incident summary once we have the full timeline.

Sorry for the disruption — we know this impacts your pipelines and appreciate the heads-up as we work it.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-02-14T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nebula Analytics - Hosted API degraded (status page + follow-up)

Thanks Marissa.

Impact details from our side: multiple scheduled batch jobs that materialize embeddings (overnight) are timing out right now; we’re seeing 30–40% failure rate on the jobs kicked off at 07:30 PT. Also seeing intermittent 502s for the live query endpoint used by our web app (not as many, but affecting some customers).

We need an ETA and a rough plan for any rollback or traffic separation you’ll do. If there’s a likely >2 hour impact, we’ll need to open a support ticket for credits per our SLA.

Can you also confirm whether any customer data was retried or duplicated due to the failures — our ingestion needs dedupe guarantees.

—Priya
Priya Sengupta
Head of Platform Reliability, Nebula Analytics
priya.s@nebulaanalytics.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nebula Analytics - Hosted API degraded (status page + follow-up)

Marissa — quick internal plan and ask for approvals:

1) Switch Nebula traffic to dedicated-capacity pool (dedicated-g4dn-1). Expected time: ~12 minutes to warm and migrate; reduces multi-tenant interference.
2) Rollback latest runtime kernel patch on us-west-2 serving ring (the patch increases attention cache compaction and appears to spike latency on >2k token requests). Rollback will take ~20 minutes and may cause short (~30s) reconnects.
3) Enable per-tenant request-level throttling (soft) for Nebula to protect their tail latency while we validate rollback.

I’ll execute items 1 and 3 immediately once Marissa approves. I’ll schedule rollback (2) with a short maintenance window and warn customers in the status page note; Rafael will monitor CPU/GPU temp and queue depths.

Quoted for context:

Date: 2026-02-14T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Nebula Analytics - Hosted API degraded (status page + follow-up)

Priya / Jake — quick update: we completed migration of Nebula traffic to a dedicated pool and enabled soft throttling on high-cost long-sequence requests. The rollback of the runtime kernel patch is in progress and currently at 40% of the serving ring; we expect it to complete in the next ~15 minutes.

Early signals look positive: error rates for Nebula have dropped from ~18% to ~4% in the last 10 minutes and median tail latency is trending down. We attached a short CSV timeline with observed error-rate and tail latency samples for your account.

Please retry the failed batch jobs on a small subset first and let us know if you continue to see duplicates — we will provide dedupe guidance if any partial retries were performed by our system.

We are continuing to monitor and I’ll post a post-incident summary once we have the full timeline and root cause analysis.

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv (text/csv)

—Marissa

Date: 2026-02-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Nebula Analytics - Post-incident summary & next steps

Hi Priya — following up with the post-incident summary and next steps. Thank you again for your patience and the quick status information yesterday; it helped us scope the tail latency issue faster.

Summary (short):
- Incident window: 2026-02-14T07:50:00-07:00 through 2026-02-14T09:15:00-07:00 (elevated 5xx and timeouts observed).
- Final mitigation: traffic moved to dedicated capacity + rollback of attention-cache kernel patch.
- Primary cause (prelim): an interaction between the kernel optimization and long-sequence cache compaction that amplified queueing for long-running requests under certain token distributions.
- Impact to Nebula: ~22% of long-sequence batch jobs retried/failed; live queries saw intermittent 502s but customer-facing surface was limited.

Next steps we propose:
- We’ve prepared a brief postmortem draft and recommended mitigations (attached and linked): https://docs.google.com/document/d/POSTMORTEMDOCID
- Follow-up actions: disable the kernel patch in the us-west ring for two weeks while we add a regression test against your token distributions; add a per-tenant long-sequence circuit breaker; and improve our status page sampling to include tenant-level tail metrics.
- Compensation: per our SLA clause, we will credit Nebula for the impacted token units for the incident window; I’ll route details to billing once you confirm the affected projects.

Would you be available for a 30-minute postmortem call tomorrow 2026-02-16 between 09:00–12:00 PT? We’ll invite engineering and your reliability team to walk through the timeline and our mitigation plan.

Apologies again for the disruption. If you want changes to the draft postmortem before the call, reply with comments or attach edits; we’ll incorporate them.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
